Target audience: High school students or early university students

Section: section_1 — Introduction: From Average to Instantaneous

Lecture lines:
Speed is distance over time.
A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds.
Average speed is 20 meters per second.
But how fast at one exact moment?
That is the challenge of instantaneous speed.

Planned animations:
Fade in title "From Average to Instantaneous".
Display an average velocity line on a curve.
Slide the interval endpoints toward each other.
Flash the secant line turning into a tangent.
Highlight the instantaneous slope at a point.

Section: section_2 — Visualizing the 'Shrinking' Interval

Lecture lines:
Two points define a secant line.
As the points get closer, the gap shrinks.
The secant line tilts as the gap closes.
At the limit, it touches one point.
This is the tangent line.

Planned animations:
Display interval [a, b] on horizontal axis.
Shrink b toward a dynamically.
Show the narrowing secant slope convergence.
Highlight the limit h approaching zero.
Transform secant segment into a tangent point.

Section: section_3 — Defining the Derivative

Lecture lines:
We define the slope as a limit.
The formula uses a difference quotient.
As h approaches zero, we get the derivative.
It maps the slope at any input x.
The derivative gives the instantaneous rate.

Planned animations:
Display the formal limit definition formula.
Color-code f(x+h) and f(x) components.
Animate the division by h expansion.
Pulse the limit notation 'lim h->0'.
Highlight the final derivative notation f'(x).

Section: section_4 — Application: Real-time Velocity

Lecture lines:
Velocity is the derivative of position.
Our robot moves at f of t equals t squared.
At three seconds, the derivative is six.
So velocity is six units per second.
Calculus measures real-world motion precisely.

Planned animations:
Show position-time graph of moving object.
Draw slope at specific time t=1.
Label result as instantaneous velocity v(t).

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Summary

Lecture lines:
We traveled from average to instantaneous.
The derivative acts as a mathematical zoom.
It gives us precision at a single point.

Planned animations:
Recap the derivative as instantaneous rate.
Review key transition: secant to tangent.
Display final derivative formula clearly.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # BASE

        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(Create(slope_line))

        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)

        self.wait(2)
